title: kortix-ai/CompanyOS — Kortix CompanyOS – the open-source operating system for your company. Multiplayer AI agents, your company as code, sovereign on your infrastructure or ours.
content:
The open-source CompanyOS: the cloud-native agent harness for companies.
Open Source · Extensible · Multiplayer · Sovereign
Always-on agents that start on events, run in parallel and share one memory of your company.
Build custom agents on pi and ship them from one git repo. Schedules, webhooks, your tools' events and your team's messages start them. My Kortix routes the work, and swarms of agents run it in parallel, each on its own cloud computer with state that persists.
Agents connect to 3,000+ apps, build and host the apps your company needs, and land every change through a review your team approves. Share agents and context across your whole team. Open source, any model, on your infrastructure or ours.
Website · Guide · Cloud · AI Transformation · Manifesto
An agent today is one chat session on one machine. It waits for a person to type. It blocks while a long job runs. Every task it takes on shares one context. It stops when the laptop sleeps. A person can follow only a few such sessions at once, so human attention runs out long before the model does.
Kortix CompanyOS takes the session out of the person's hands. It is a cloud-native agent harness: you write custom agents on pi, an open-source agent harness, and Kortix deploys them to the cloud and supplies everything around the agent loop that one session cannot.
  You, in the web app             Slack · Teams · email        Events
        │                         threads                      schedules · webhooks
        ▼                              │                       app + connector events
 ┌─────────────┐                       │                       change requests · loops
 │  My Kortix  │ answers at once,      │                              │
 │             │ never blocks          │                       ┌──────┴──────┐
 └──────┬──────┘                       │                       │  Triggers   │ filter in code,
        │ hands off in the background  │                       └──────┬──────┘ then start or wake
        ▼                              ▼                              ▼
 ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
 │ Agent sessions: custom pi agents, each on its own cloud computer       │
 │ hand-offs · workflows · messages between sessions · reports back       │
 └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                                     │
                                     │ sleeps when idle, wakes with its full history
                                     ▼
   State that persists: git repo · Drive · /workspace · session record
   What lands on main goes through a change request a person approves
Connect your company's tools once, and every agent and every teammate works with them, with the same skills and the same company memory. Your agents, skills, memory and connectors live in one git repo you own: your whole company as code. Any model, your own keys, on Kortix Cloud, in your VPC or on your own on-prem network.
One system, from the message that starts the work to the change that lands it.
An operating system is the layer everything on a computer runs on. A CompanyOS is that layer for a company: the place its AI agents do the work, and the rules they work under.
kortix.yaml declares all of it, and every agent, skill and rule is a file in one repo you own.
That is your company as code.
Outcome ──> Plan ──> Work ──> Verify ──> Learn ──┐
   ^                                             │
   └──────────── the next run starts there ──────┘
- Outcome. You state it once, in plain words, with the rules that matter.
- Plan. An agent owns it end to end, breaks it into work and wakes itself on a schedule.
- Work. Agents run on their own cloud computers at any hour, started by schedules, webhooks and your tools.
- Verify. A separate agent checks the result, and changes land through a change request you approve.
- Learn. What the agents learned goes back into company memory and skills. Every run makes the next one better.
Thousands of agents can run in parallel on one config. How outcomes work →
Three commands. Build your company like a codebase, then bring it live.
# 1 · Install the CLI
curl -fsSL https://kortix.com/install | bash
# 2 · Scaffold a project: kortix.yaml plus your agents, skills and runtime config
kortix init
# 3 · Ship it: push the repo and bring the whole thing live in the cloud
kortix ship
From here:
kortix sessions new --prompt "Summarize this week's commits and open a change request"
kortix cr ls          # review what an agent proposes, merge to keep it
kortix chat           # talk to a session's agent from your terminal
No setup: sign up at kortix.com, create a project and start a session. The Guide walks you through Kortix CompanyOS from A to Z.
- SciencePal, the AI research assistant of the Hong Kong Institute of AI for Science at City University of Hong Kong, built from Kortix's open-source code.
- Platinum, a sandbox cloud for AI agents, built and tested by agents on Kortix.
- Kortix itself: an intake agent triages every issue and worker agents fix it on their own machines.
- An AI-run hedge fund desk, our own, on real public SEC data with simulated capital.
- A US telecommunications infrastructure company whose agents design fiber routes, self-hosted in its own cloud.
- An international executive search firm, rebuilt around agents.
- WRITER, the enterprise AI platform, built from Kortix's open-source code.
- Wring, autonomous AWS cost optimization.
Kortix CompanyOS is self-hosting native: one Docker Compose stack in your cloud account, your VPC or on your own servers, from the same images the managed cloud runs.
curl -fsSL https://kortix.com/install | bash
kortix self-host start
kortix hosts use selfhost  # ↔  kortix hosts use cloud
The first run asks six things and no model key. You connect GitHub and add model keys in the app afterwards. Agent sandboxes run on the provider you configure (Platinum by default), and the stack pulls its images from Docker Hub, so this is a self-hosted install, not a disconnected one. Self-hosting guide →
One isolated machine per session · per-resource permissions for people and agents · roles, groups and an audit trail · SAML 2.0 single sign-on and SCIM 2.0 · connector credentials held server-side · secrets encrypted at rest with a key per project · merge deny-by-default for agents · approval rules you set · Kortix Cloud, your VPC or on-prem. SOC 2 Type I verified. Security →
Don't want to build it yourself? Our team maps your company, unifies your data, automates the work with agents, builds your custom apps and trains your team, all on Kortix CompanyOS, in a repo you own. kortix.com/services
Kortix stays open source. A free white-label license lets you run it under your own name and logo, in your own structure, and as a hosted service for your customers. The one requirement: use Platinum as your exclusive compute provider for everything it offers, at rates we commit to keep competitive. Sign online and you are licensed on the spot: WHITE-LABEL-LICENSE.md. Custom terms: marko@kortix.ai.
pnpm install
pnpm dev            # web + API (scripts/dev-local.sh)
pnpm dev:web        # web app only
pnpm dev:api        # API only
pnpm dev:sandbox    # build the local sandbox image
pnpm build          # build all packages
pnpm nuke           # tear down the local Docker environment
Apps live under apps/ (web, api, cli, desktop-electron, mobile, sandbox). The Guide
and the developer reference are in apps/web/content/docs. The whole platform ships under one
version (root VERSION): API, frontend, CLI and desktop release together as vX.Y.Z.
Local secrets, test lanes and the PR loop: CONTRIBUTING.md. Issues and pull requests are welcome.
We are building the Operating System for SuperIntelligence: for companies run by AI, owned end to end.

report.summary: Kortix launches CompanyOS, an open-source cloud-native harness that deploys always-on, parallel AI agents with shared memory, letting companies run as code on their own infrastructure.
report.background: AI agents today are mostly single chat sessions tied to one machine: they wait for a human prompt, block on long jobs, share one context, and stop when a laptop sleeps. Human attention, not model capacity, becomes the bottleneck. Meanwhile enterprises want agents that work across teams, tools, and schedules while remaining secure and auditable. Open-source agent frameworks such as LangChain, CrewAI, and AutoGen have emerged, but few package orchestration, persistent cloud sandboxes, company-wide memory, connectors, and governance into one deployable system. Kortix, known for its open-source AI agent platform, positions CompanyOS as the layer above individual agents: a git-based, self-hostable operating system for running many agents as company infrastructure, with human approval and sovereign deployment options.
key_points: Always-on multiplayer agents: CompanyOS starts custom agents from schedules, webhooks, app events, Slack, Teams, or email. Each session runs on its own cloud computer, can run in parallel, hands off work, persists state, sleeps when idle, and wakes with full history. My Kortix answers immediately and routes work in the background, removing the single-session bottleneck.

Company as code: Agents, skills, memory, connectors, and rules live in one git repo declared by kortix.yaml. The CLI scaffolds and ships the stack with kortix init and kortix ship. Agent changes land through reviewable change requests that a person approves, and lessons from each run feed back into company memory.

Sovereign and model-flexible: Users can bring any model and their own API keys, running on Kortix Cloud, in a VPC, or on-prem. Self-hosting uses one Docker Compose stack from the same images. Security features include per-session isolation, role-based permissions, audit trails, SAML/SCIM, server-side connector credentials, encrypted secrets, and deny-by-default merges for agents.

Real-world use cases: Kortix cites SciencePal at City University of Hong Kong, Platinum sandbox cloud, an AI-run hedge fund desk on SEC data, a telecom company designing fiber routes, an executive search firm, WRITER, and AWS cost optimization. Agents connect to 3,000+ apps and can build and host internal apps.

Open-source with a white-label twist: The platform remains open source, but a free white-label license requires using Platinum as the exclusive compute provider for everything it offers. That keeps the core available while tying commercial rebranding to Kortix's sandbox infrastructure.
report.impact: CompanyOS signals a shift from single-session copilots to agent orchestration platforms: the competitive layer becomes the harness, memory, permissions, and deployment model around the model. For the AI industry, it pressures vendors to offer self-hosted, multi-agent systems with auditability and human approval, not just chat interfaces. For developers, it introduces a git-based agent-operations workflow and a new skill set around agent configs, sandboxes, and change requests, though the Platinum white-label condition raises lock-in questions. For regular users, agents appear inside Slack, Teams, and email, handling work continuously while humans approve changes, which improves leverage but makes oversight, security, and clear approval rules essential.
report.tools: Try Kortix CompanyOS via kortix init and kortix ship, or self-host with Docker Compose. Watch the pi agent harness, Platinum sandbox cloud, and Kortix CLI. For comparison, evaluate LangGraph, CrewAI, AutoGen, and OpenHands for agent orchestration, plus MCP connectors for tool access. Start with a small repo, one scheduled agent, and a human-approved change request before scaling to parallel swarms.
